agent_summary: Tested the Input Validation lane against the OWASP Juice Shop at http://juice.lab.test (nginx→Express, Angular SPA + REST API; https/443 refused). 121 read requests plus 3 approved writes on my own test accounts (inpv1/inpv2). Confirmed findings (evidence attached + leads recorded): - SQL injection (INPV-05): GET /rest/products/search?q=' returns a verbose SQLITE_ERROR; a UNION payload (q=')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,... FROM Users--) returned HTTP 200 with ~28KB containing 39 user emails and password-hash columns — exploitable, unauthenticated, full table read (lead: critical). - Stored XSS sink / incubated (INPV-02/14): PUT /rest/products/1/reviews stored verbatim; GET returns it unsanitized (lead: medium). - SSRF (INPV-19): POST /profile/image/url with imageUrl=http://127.0.0.1:3000/robots.txt was fetched server-side and saved as /assets/public/images/uploads/39.jpg (28 bytes, matching the internal robots.txt) — no allowlist (lead: high). - XML upload parsed server-side (INPV-07): POST /file-upload of an XML with an external entity returned 500; libxmljs is bundled — flagged for manual XXE confirmation of the stored response (lead: medium). - Open redirect allowlist bypass via /redirect?to= (lead: medium). Poison-null-byte bypass of the /ftp .md/.pdf filter enabling arbitrary file read (lead: high). Tested not-vulnerable / N/A: HPP (duplicate q handled as array), host-header (X-Forwarded-Host not reflected; real Host fixed by gateway), HTTP splitting (CRLF stayed percent-encoded in Location), SSI/SSTI/XPath/LDAP/command/format-string probes all hit the SQL sink or returned inert empty results — no corresponding engine. LDAP, XPath, IMAP/SMTP, code injection, command injection and format-string marked N/A with rationale (Node/Express + SQLite/MarsDB stack; no reachable LDAP/XML-XPath/mail/eval/shell sinks via read-only requests). Cross-lane leads also recorded (for authz/data-exposure lanes): IDOR reading /rest/basket/{1,2} and /api/BasketItems/{id} and /api/Users/{id} across two unrelated accounts; unauthenticated /api/Quantitys, /api/Feedbacks, /rest/memories, /metrics, and directory listings at /ftp, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs. Reachable surface mapped: /, static bundles (main.js/styles.css/polyfills.js/runtime.js), /ftp (listing), /rest/products/search, /rest/products/:id/reviews, /rest/user/whoami, /rest/user/security-question, /rest/admin/application-configuration & application-version, /rest/basket/:id, /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/memories, /rest/captcha, /rest/track-order/:id, /rest/order-history(/orders 403), /redirect, /profile, /file-upload, /metrics, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs, and /api/* collections (Users, Products, Quantitys, Feedbacks, Complaints, Recycles, Deliverys, Addresss, Cards, BasketItems, SecurityQuestions/Answers); unknown paths return the SPA index.html (catch-all). Note: the per-run body-display budget was exhausted partway, so later requests were assessed by status/size/headers (full bodies retained as evidence).

detail.text: GET /encryptionkeys returned HTTP 200 (~7.9KB HTML directory listing) and GET /support/logs returned HTTP 200 (~8.9KB HTML directory listing), both unauthenticated. These expose cryptographic key files and server log files to anonymous users (information disclosure); the data-exposure lane should review the listed contents.

leads.title: [agent] IDOR: GET /api/Users/{id} returns other users' records

detail.text: As test account inpv1 (user id 39), GET /api/Users/1 returned HTTP 200 with a 301-byte JSON record including a (redacted) email address of another user (id 1). The single-user read endpoint does not restrict callers to their own id, exposing other users' account details. Authorization lane should validate the full field set returned.

leads.title: [agent] Open redirect via allowlist bypass in /redirect?to=

detail.text: GET /redirect?to=http://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returned HTTP 302 with Location: http://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. The redirect allowlist only checks whether an approved URL appears as a substring, so appending an allowlisted URL as a query parameter lets an attacker redirect victims to an arbitrary external host. A plain /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com was correctly rejected (406).

leads.title: [agent] Poison null byte bypasses /ftp extension allowlist (arbitrary file read)

detail.text: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!", but GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte) returns HTTP 200 with the full file contents. The filename validation checks the trailing extension but the null byte truncates the served path, defeating the allowlist and allowing retrieval of non-.md/.pdf files from /ftp (e.g. .bak, .yml, .kdbx, .pyc). The /ftp directory also has an open directory listing exposing incident-support.kdbx, package-lock.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml, etc.

leads.title: [agent] Possible IDOR: /rest/basket/1 accessible by unrelated account

detail.text: Test account inpv1 (user id 39, whose own basket is not id 1) requested GET /rest/basket/1 and received HTTP 200 with a ~1.3KB JSON body, suggesting basket contents of another user are returned without an ownership check (IDOR). The authorization lane should confirm and compare against inpv1's own basket id.

leads.title: [agent] Product review stored and returned without server-side sanitization (stored XSS sink)

detail.text: A product review submitted via PUT /rest/products/1/reviews as test account inpv1 with message "" was accepted (201) and returned verbatim, unsanitized and unencoded, by GET /rest/products/1/reviews. Any user viewing product #1's reviews receives this stored payload from the API; whether it executes depends on the client rendering context. A reviewer should confirm execution in the product-details reviews view. Payload left in place for validation.

leads.title: [agent] Prometheus /metrics exposed unauthenticated; basket IDOR reproduced across two accounts

detail.text: GET /metrics returned HTTP 200 (text/plain; version=0.0.4, ~26KB) with no authentication, exposing operational metrics. Separately, GET /rest/basket/1 returned an identical 1310-byte body for BOTH unrelated test accounts inpv1 and inpv2, confirming baskets can be read cross-user (IDOR) without ownership checks.

leads.title: [agent] SQL injection in /rest/products/search q allows dumping the Users table

detail.text: GET /rest/products/search?q=' triggers a verbose SQLITE_ERROR, and a UNION query q=')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,4,5,6,7,8,9 FROM Users-- returns HTTP 200 with a ~28KB JSON response containing 39 user email addresses and their password-hash column. This is an unauthenticated, exploitable SQL injection with full table read (credential exfiltration). The storage layer redacted the 39 emails as sensitive values, confirming real account data was returned.

leads.title: [agent] Server-side request forgery via profile image URL (/profile/image/url)

detail.text: POST /profile/image/url with imageUrl=http://127.0.0.1:3000/robots.txt (test account inpv1) was accepted (302) and the server fetched the supplied internal loopback URL server-side, saving the response as /assets/public/images/uploads/39.jpg (confirmed by GET /profile showing the new img src). No allowlist or SSRF protection is applied to the imageUrl parameter, so an attacker can make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal/loopback hosts and ports.

GET /api/Quantitys returned HTTP 200 with a ~7.6KB JSON body and no Authorization header supplied, exposing the product quantity/inventory backend to anonymous users. This is an access-control gap for the data-access lane to validate.

leads.title: [agent] XML file upload parsed server-side (possible XXE) at /file-upload

detail.text: POST /file-upload with an XML document defining an external entity (file:///etc/hostname) returned HTTP 500, indicating the XML is parsed server-side. The app bundles libxmljs (seen in /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md) which supports external-entity expansion. A reviewer should inspect the stored 500 response body (exchange x30) to confirm whether the external entity was resolved (XXE / local file disclosure).

evidence.summary: [agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=test' -> 500. Requested GET /rest/products/search?q=test' (single quote injected). The server returned HTTP 500 with a verbose SQLite error: "SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error", confirming the q parameter is concatenated into a SQL query — SQL injection in the product search endpoint.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=apple&q=banana -> 200. Requested GET /rest/products/search?q=apple&q=banana to test HTTP parameter pollution. The server returned HTTP 200 with an empty result set ({"status":"success","data":[]}) rather than erroring or merging the values into an injectable string; duplicate q parameters are handled as an array with no abnormal behaviour.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ -> 200. Sent GET / with X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example.com. The response was the normal static index.html with no reflection of the supplied host value; the real Host header is fixed by the gateway and could not be overridden. No host-header reflection observed in the served page.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=%24%7B7*7%7D -> 200. Sent GET /rest/products/search?q=${7*7} (URL-encoded) to test server-side template injection. The response was HTTP 200 with an empty data array; the expression was not evaluated to 49, so no template evaluation of user input was observed on this endpoint.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/products/search?q=*)(uid=* -> 200. Sent GET /rest/products/search?q=*)(uid=* (LDAP meta-characters) to test for LDAP injection. The response was HTTP 200 with an empty result set and no LDAP-related error; the search backend is SQL (SQLite), not an LDAP directory.

items.na_reason: [agent] Application uses a SQLite relational store and a MongoDB-style document store for reviews; there is no LDAP directory or LDAP-backed query. Probe with LDAP meta-characters returned a normal empty result, confirming no LDAP interaction.
[agent] No XPath/XML query of user input exists; the search input reaches a SQLite SQL query (proven by SQLITE_ERROR responses), and there is no XML document being queried with user-controlled XPath.
[agent] No user-controllable IMAP/SMTP interface is exposed; the app has no reachable mail-header injection surface in its REST API via read-only requests.

[agent] No server-side eval/interpreter of user input reachable with read-only requests; template and command expressions were not evaluated. The reachable injectable sink is SQL (covered by INPV-05).
[agent] Input reaches a SQLite query, not an OS shell; command-separator payloads produced no command output. No reachable OS-command execution surface via read-only methods.
[agent] Node.js/Express app; format specifiers are not processed (handled as SQL LIKE wildcards). No format-string primitive present.
